If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/moran_global_2022_no2.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = ADJACENCY_PATH

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop missing NO2 values
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['NO2_value']).reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df_clean['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)

# Build adjacency matrix for valid boroughs
W = np.zeros((n, n))
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    a, b = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    if a in borough_to_idx and b in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[a]
        j = borough_to_idx[b]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1

# Row standardize
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
W_std = W / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Compute Moran's I
x = df_clean['NO2_value'].values
z = x - x.mean()

numerator = 0.0
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        numerator += W_std[i, j] * z[i] * z[j]

denominator = np.sum(z ** 2)
S0 = W_std.sum()

moran_I = (n / S0) * (numerator / denominator)

print('n:', n)
print('S0:', S0)
print('Numerator:', numerator)
print('Denominator:', denominator)
print('Morans I:', moran_I)
print('Expected under randomization:', -1/(n-1))

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 1000
perm_stats = np.zeros(n_perm)

for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    num_perm = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            num_perm += W_std[i, j] * z_perm[i] * z_perm[j]
    perm_stats[p] = (n / S0) * (num_perm / denominator)

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = np.mean(np.abs(perm_stats) >= np.abs(moran_I))
print('Permutation p-value (two-tailed):', p_value)
print('Mean of permutations:', perm_stats.mean())
print('Std of permutations:', perm_stats.std())
print('Min perm:', perm_stats.min())
print('Max perm:', perm_stats.max())
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/moran_global_2022_no2.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = ADJACENCY_PATH

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop missing NO2 values
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['NO2_value']).reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df_clean['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)

# Build adjacency matrix for valid boroughs
W = np.zeros((n, n))
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    a, b = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    if a in borough_to_idx and b in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[a]
        j = borough_to_idx[b]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1

# Row standardize
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
W_std = W / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Compute Moran's I using matrix notation
x = df_clean['NO2_value'].values
z = x - x.mean()

S0 = W_std.sum()
moran_I = (n / S0) * (z.T @ W_std @ z) / (z.T @ z)

print('S0:', S0)
print('Morans I (matrix):', moran_I)

# Verify with loop
numerator = 0.0
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        numerator += W_std[i, j] * z[i] * z[j]
moran_I_loop = (n / S0) * (numerator / np.sum(z**2))
print('Morans I (loop):', moran_I_loop)

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles - one-tailed for clustering
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 1000
perm_stats = np.zeros(n_perm)

for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    perm_stats[p] = (n / S0) * (z_perm.T @ W_std @ z_perm) / (z.T @ z)

# One-tailed p-value (for positive clustering)
p_one_tailed = np.mean(perm_stats >= moran_I)
# Two-tailed p-value
p_two_tailed = np.mean(np.abs(perm_stats) >= np.abs(moran_I))

print('One-tailed p-value:', p_one_tailed)
print('Two-tailed p-value:', p_two_tailed)
print('Expected Moran I under null:', -1/(n-1))
print('Observed Moran I:', moran_I)

# Summary stats of permutations
print('Perm mean:', perm_stats.mean())
print('Perm std:', perm_stats.std())
print('Perm min:', perm_stats.min())
print('Perm max:', perm_stats.max())
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/moran_global_2022_no2.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = ADJACENCY_PATH

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop missing NO2 values
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['NO2_value']).reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df_clean['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)

# Check name matching
no2_names = set(df_clean['borough'])
adj_names = set(adj['borough']) | set(adj['neighbor'])
print('Names in NO2 but not adjacency:', no2_names - adj_names)
print('Names in adjacency but not NO2:', adj_names - no2_names)

# Build adjacency matrix for valid boroughs
W = np.zeros((n, n))
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    a, b = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    if a in borough_to_idx and b in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[a]
        j = borough_to_idx[b]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1

# Row standardize
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
W_std = W / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Compute Moran's I
x = df_clean['NO2_value'].values
z = x - x.mean()

S0 = W_std.sum()
moran_I = (n / S0) * (z.T @ W_std @ z) / (z.T @ z)

print('Morans I:', moran_I)

# Compute spatial lag correlation
lag = W_std @ z
spatial_corr = np.corrcoef(z, lag)[0, 1]
print('Spatial lag correlation:', spatial_corr)

# Permutation test with 2000 shuffles
np.random.seed(123)
n_perm = 2000
perm_stats = np.zeros(n_perm)

for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    perm_stats[p] = (n / S0) * (z_perm.T @ W_std @ z_perm) / (z.T @ z)

p_two_tailed = np.mean(np.abs(perm_stats) >= np.abs(moran_I))
p_positive = np.mean(perm_stats >= moran_I)

print('Two-tailed p-value (2000 perm):', p_two_tailed)
print('P(I_perm >= observed):', p_positive)
print('Perm mean:', perm_stats.mean())
print('Perm std:', perm_stats.std())

# Check a few high/low value boroughs and their neighbors
df_clean_sorted = df_clean.sort_values('NO2_value', ascending=False)
print('\nTop 5 NO2 boroughs:')
print(df_clean_sorted.head())
print('\nBottom 5 NO2 boroughs:')
print(df_clean_sorted.tail())

# Show neighbors and their values for highest and lowest
for target in [df_clean_sorted.iloc[0]['borough'], df_clean_sorted.iloc[-1]['borough']]:
    idx = borough_to_idx[target]
    neighbor_indices = np.where(W[idx] == 1)[0]
    neighbor_names = [boroughs[j] for j in neighbor_indices]
    neighbor_values = [x[j] for j in neighbor_indices]
    print(f'\n{target} NO2: {x[idx]:.4f}')
    print('Neighbors:', list(zip(neighbor_names, neighbor_values)))
    print('Neighbor mean:', np.mean(neighbor_values))
```
